correctness.rationale: In the four-regular cycle square, initial induced degree at most two at all blue vertices permits no first force. A blue vertex with three or four blue neighbors fills its closed neighborhood, which consists of five consecutive cyclic vertices. In any proper maximal blue interval containing these five, the penultimate vertex can force the next vertex beyond the interval, so propagation reaches the whole graph. The length-five window test therefore describes exactly the failed sets for n≥7. Four-bit states give one closed walk with fixed time origin per labeled valid word, of weight z to the number of blue vertices. I reproduced det(I−uT) independently by sparse signed Laplace expansion, obtaining exactly 1−u−zu²−z²u³−z³u⁵+z⁴u⁷+z⁵u⁸. The negative logarithmic derivative in u, multiplied by u, gives the trace numerator and hence the failed-set coefficients; subtracting from (1+z)^n gives the forcing polynomial. Only coefficients n≥7 are interpreted as graph enumerators. At size four, the center plus three neighbors gives 4n presentations; two centers at distance one require the two remaining vertices to be the other consecutive common neighbors, and centers at distance two have only one common neighbor for n≥7. Thus only the n consecutive four-sets are counted twice, and they have exactly two centers. The crossing-edge bound gives 2|S|≤4(n−|S|) for failed S; the stated cyclic words attain the floor by the local test, including both residue boundaries. The packaged Newton-identity checker and recorded n=7 through 14 census were inspected, not run; the unrestricted result follows from propagation and the fixed-size formal calculation.

evidence: Let a=u, b=zu², c=z²u³, d=z³u⁴ be the weights of gaps 1,2,3,4; a gap contributes its length to n and length minus one to blue cardinality. In order 1,2,3,4, use destination weights in the gap-transition matrix A with rows (a,b,c,d), (a,b,c,0), (a,b,c,0), (a,0,0,0). These are exactly the other record's allowed cyclic gap words.

For m white vertices the trace of A^m counts ordered gap tuples. To count the subsets of labeled residues, distinguish a white start in each set: n choices of starting residue for each tuple and m representations per set, giving factor n/m even for periodic tuples.

Thus the failed-set series, in orders n≥7, is the corresponding part of u∂_u sum_{m≥1} tr(A^m)/m = −u∂_u log det(I−A). The determinant reduces by merging equivalent states 2 and 3 to 1−a−b−c−ad+ad(b+c), precisely D(u,z). Its derivative is exactly the frozen numerator divided by D.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The frozen propagation lemma makes every failure an initial stall. Hence its whole failed family is exactly the complements of the other record's forts. For these forts, every vertex outside has at least one neighbor inside because all gaps are at most four; the fort condition raises this to at least two, equivalent to induced blue degree at most two. The empty blue set corresponds to the full white fort; the full blue set is successful. This compares the same ordinary color rule, labels, and full range n≥7.

originality.rationale: The strongest distinct indexed comparison, a06a1735df72, gives an all-forts gap law on the identical labeled cycle square throughout the frozen range. Every stalled initial blue set has a nonempty white complement that is itself a fort, and conversely a white fort makes the blue complement failed. Thus the other record's rule is equivalent to the full set classification, not merely to the numerical largest-failed-size corollary. Moreover the exact frozen rational function is a direct weighted cyclic-word evaluation of that very rule; the implication is exhibited below. The rational form is not stated verbatim in the comparison record. This is a decision on demonstrable coverage in the inspected corpus, not an attribution of historical priority or a claim that the later-displayed record preceded the frozen one.
